From: Ron Hall, SOUTHSEA

Dear Ron and Brian,

I've been subscribing to OUTLET
for some months now and I felt I
must write and say how good it
is. My set up is a Spectrum 128,
+D, 3.5" disc drive, Brother HR5
printer and Ferguson mono
monitor. I am, however, having
problems with a couple of your
recent routines.

1."Minichars 4" for Wordmaster.
However I try to load it into
Wordmaster, my only result is
"File not Found 0.2". You say
put WM in drive 1 and use "CLEAR
5E4:etc. Do you really mean just
put the disc in and do nothing

else but type line above or do
you load WM, access BASIC then
type the command? However I do
it the result is the same error
code. As I am very new to
computing and one of your older
members (late 50's) I would very
much appreciate some detailed
help or at least a pointer in
the right way.

2."OUTPRINT". I only seem to be
able to get this to work in 3
columns in the Wide and Fast
mode. Wide print and Micro prod-
uce rubbish. When just copying
the screen page it works in Mini
and Norm both thick and thin
modes. I am sending a copy of
this to Mike Haine for his
comments.

Keep up the Good work and it is
smashing to be able to now use
OUTLET in 128 mode.
               Yours Sincerely,
                   Ron Hall.

Thanks Ron. We're dependant on
Mike Haine to resolve these
OUTPRINT problems. On the mini-
chars problem, yes, you do NOT
need to LOAD WM first. Alter the
5E4 to 5E3 then replace "COPY"
with CHR$ 255 as I suspect you
may be trying to LOAD in 128K
BASIC (which won't accept the
keyword COPY). If that still
doesn't work, do a CAT and check
the name of the WM code to see
if it is different. Let me know
if it still doesn't work.
                        - Brian

a calculation like CHR$ (35+35).

To: Mr. R.W. Jeffs from Brian

Yes,CODESHIFTER is a very useful
program but it's worth repeating
here that it will not work on
100% of code.

To set a TAB position from TAS-
EXTRAS,you move the cursor along
a line to the column you want to
tab, select EXTENDED MODE then
press T. Any number of TABs can
be thus selected from 1 to 64.
Each selected TAB will be shown
with a small marker at the foot
of the screen.

To use the TABs, simply press
INVERSE VIDEO (CAPS SHIFT + 4)
and the cursor will move to the
right to the next TAB. This

REPLACES the "move to the start
of the next word" function which
you usually get with INVERSE
VIDEO.


To switch OFF any TAB, just move
the cursor to the position of
the TAB and select EXTENDED MODE
and then press T again.To switch
off ALL the TABs,select EXTENDED
MODE then Q after which the
normal INVERSE VIDEO function
will return.


There is no simple solution to
your BASPEEK query but I've made
a note to see if the program can
be modified.

Now, INSTAMATCHIT WILL find ALL
occurrences of the word COMET if
you search for COM so you should
check your program or send in a
a copy on tape and I will check
it for you. Perhaps your entries
are in small letters and you are
entering capitals or vice versa?
However, it will also find ALL
occurrences of COM even if they
occur in the middle of a name
such as BEACHCOMBERS LTD. For
this reason it is not suitable
to list all names beginning with
A as it will list EVERY SINGLE
WORD containing an A! One way
might be to write a routine to
search for say, PA and discard
any find which is not the first
two characters of the element,eg
IF A$(N, TO 2)<>"PA" THEN NEXT N

You would obviously substitute
your input string for "PA"in the
above and the LEN of your input
string for the 2 in the bracket.

The solution to your LPRINT
problem is as follows: LPRINT is
short for PRINT #3 whereas PRINT
is short for PRINT #2.If you use
a variable in place of the 2 and
3 you can both PRINT to the
screen then to your printer. Eg.

 FOR S = 2 TO 3
 PRINT #S;"TEXT" (or A$ etc)
 NEXT S

This will print TEXT on screen
then print it on your printer.

Let me know if you need further
clarification.        - Brian.

To Ken Bates from Brian
Try this for the Kempston Mouse:
100 LET Y=10 : LET X=10
150 LET S$=SCREEN$(Y,X)
200 PRINT AT Y,X;"<"
300 IF IN 64479=1 AND Y THEN
 PRINT AT Y,X;S$:LET Y=Y-1:GO TO
 150
400 IF IN 64479=255 AND Y<21
 THEN PRINT AT Y,X;S$:LET Y=Y+1:
 GO TO 150
500 IF IN 65503=1 AND X THEN
 PRINT AT Y,X;S$:LET X=X-1: GO
 TO 150
600 IF IN 65503=255 AND X<31
 THEN PRINT AT Y,X;S$:LET X=X+1:
 GO TO 150
700 IF IN 64223=254 THEN GO SUB
   1000:REM RIGHT BUTTON ROUTINE
800 IF IN 64423=253 THEN GO SUB
   2000:REM LEFT BUTTON ROUTINE
900 GO TO 200

It may be that 64223 and 64423
in lines 700 and 800 should be
the same but they are as shown
in your letter.You may also need
to reverse the 1 and 255 in
lines 500 and 600 and the 253
and 254 in lines 700 and 800.

You may find however, that BASIC
is rather slow and cannot keep
up with the mouse. Write again
if you need further help, say
with the push-button routines.If
anyone has better routines write
in or direct to Ken. please also
contact Ken with info on CP/M.

                   - Brian

From: Steven Watkins, NUNEATON

Thank you for printing my letter
concerning the SERIAL 8056
printer in issue 25. Before I go
any further I feel that I should
make a few points clear: 1.The
8056 manual states it has no
graphics mode-it was only CRASH
and other magazines that stated
you could dump full screen
graphics with it. 2.The +D has a
printer port but the 8056 uses
the +2 printer port. 3.I have
not enclosed a copy of the
manual because I have managed to
dump graphics!

For the benefit of any other
8056 owner using the +2 printer
port(and to my knowledge there


are quite a few) here's how to
convert Col 80+ and the hi-res
dump from Cosinfantuttifrutti...


1.Col 80+. MERGE in the BASIC
program in 128K BASIC. Make the
following changes to the
program:


Line 9856 change FORMAT "B";BD
to FORMAT "P";BD. Change all of
line 9887 to: POKE 23349, 39:
POKE 23350,1: GOSUB VAL "9895":
RETURN


The pokes allow control codes to
get to the printer without being
removed by the +2 Printer port.

2.Cosinfantuttifrutti. MERGE in
the BASIC again and alter the
FORMAT command in line 9758 as
in Col 80+ then change line 9870
to: POKE 23349,39: POKE 23350,1:
GOSUB VAL "9795": RETURN

If you run this you will find
gaps appear in between each line
so add LPRINT CHR$ VAL "27";
CHR$ VAL "48": to the beginning

Yes,CODESHIFTER is a very useful program but it's worth repeating here that it will not work on 100% of code.

To set a TAB position from TAS- EXTRAS,you move the cursor along a line to the column you want to tab, select EXTENDED MODE then press T. Any number of TABs can be thus selected from 1 to 64. Each selected TAB will be shown with a small marker at the foot of the screen.

To use the TABs, simply press INVERSE VIDEO (CAPS SHIFT + 4) and the cursor will move to the right to the next TAB. This

REPLACES the "move to the start of the next word" function which you usually get with INVERSE VIDEO.

To switch OFF any TAB, just move the cursor to the position of the TAB and select EXTENDED MODE and then press T again.To switch off ALL the TABs,select EXTENDED MODE then Q after which the normal INVERSE VIDEO function will return.

There is no simple solution to your BASPEEK query but I've made a note to see if the program can be modified.

Now, INSTAMATCHIT WILL find ALL occurrences of the word COMET if you search for COM so you should check your program or send in a a copy on tape and I will check it for you. You would obviously substitute your input string for "PA"in the above and the LEN of your input string for the 2 in the bracket.

The solution to your LPRINT problem is as follows: LPRINT is short for PRINT #3 whereas PRINT is short for PRINT #2.If you use a variable in place of the 2 and 3 you can both PRINT to the screen then to your printer. Eg.

FOR S = 2 TO 3 PRINT #S;"TEXT" (or A$ etc) NEXT S

IF A$(N, TO 2)<>"PA" THEN NEXT N

```text
FOR S = 2 TO 3
PRINT #S;"TEXT" (или A$ и т.д.)
NEXT S
```

Это напечатает текст на экране, а затем отправит его на принтер.
